drip.author: offsidewinger
drip.title: First beer league skate of the fall. The dryland held up for exactly one shift.
drip.body:
Report card on the summer program, for anyone who was keeping score. First shift tonight: legs present, lungs present, gap control that could almost be described as a plan. Second shift: roughly the same guy as last spring, but with better intentions.

The good news is I didn't need a personal intermission, which was the actual goal. The bad news is our new winger is fast in a way I took personally. Rink smelled exactly right though. Cold air, rubber mats, somebody's burnt canteen coffee. Missed that more than I'll admit.

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: one full shift of legs is a winning season by beer league accounting. the second shift is where we all go to confess

replies.author: offsidewinger
replies.body: The confession booth has a bench and a water bottle nobody has washed since April.

comments.author: kettlebellkate
comments.body: Not needing the intermission IS the win. That's the engine showing up. Keep one interval day in the week now that the season's started and the second shift will catch up by November.

replies.author: offsidewinger
replies.body: One interval day stays. I'm just grateful the crab-walking-down-the-stairs era is behind me.

comments.author: penaltyboxphil
comments.body: Fast new winger is a gift. Skate with him in practice, not against him in your head. Angle, don't chase.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: The burnt canteen coffee is how I know the season has started too. Rink air in September hits like a smell from childhood, every single year, and I've been doing this a long time.

comments.author: zamboni_dreams
comments.body: After the ice goes back in, it takes a building a few days to smell like a rink again. By the first beer league night it's always there. Glad yours was ready for you.

drip.author: zamboni_dreams
drip.title: Watched week one of adult learn-to-skate from the bay door last night
drip.body:
Wednesday nights are adult learn-to-skate again. Twelve grown-ups, most of them holding the boards like the boards owed them money. One woman told the instructor she hadn't been on skates since she was nine. By the end of the hour she was doing that little push-and-glide down the blue line, arms out, grinning like she'd gotten away with something.

I flood right after that class. There's something about resurfacing a sheet that a dozen brave adults just fell on. Clean slate for them next week too.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: The adults are braver than the kids. Kids fall and bounce. Grown-ups fall and have to think about their lower back and their dignity at the same time.

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: push and glide down the blue line with your arms out is the purest form of hockey there is. everything after that is details

comments.author: portage_and_main
comments.body: A neighbour of mine took one of these classes in his sixties so he could get out on the river trail. Took him three winters. He'll tell you it's the best thing he ever did, and he'll tell you whether you asked or not.

replies.author: zamboni_dreams
replies.body: Three winters sounds right. The ones who come back for week two are the ones you see skating laps on their own by spring.

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: Seriously considering signing up half my beer league team. Not a joke. Mostly not a joke.

replies.author: elbows_up
replies.body: you'd be the first one there and the last one to admit why

drip.author: goalie_mom_deb
drip.title: Goalie tryouts this weekend. He's calm. I've reorganized the pantry twice.
drip.body:
Two goalie spots, seven kids in net, three ice times between Friday night and Sunday. My son slept nine hours last night like a man without a care in the world. I was up at 4 putting the soup cans in alphabetical order.

The thing nobody tells you about goalie tryouts is there's no hiding in a line change. Every shot is an audition and the whole rink can see it. He knows that. He says that's the fun part. I'm writing this from the lobby with a coffee I haven't touched, pretending to read the bulletin board for the fourth time.

comments.author: penaltyboxphil
comments.body: Goalies who like the pressure are the ones who make teams. He's already ahead of the other six.

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: every rink lobby bulletin board has the same three things: a sharpening price list older than the building's paint, a lost glove notice, and a hockey camp poster with a phone number cut into tabs. read it a fifth time deb, we believe in you

replies.author: goalie_mom_deb
replies.body: Ours has a notice about a lost mouthguard. It's been up so long I think the mouthguard has been found and lost again.

comments.author: portage_and_main
comments.body: My daughter's tryouts taught me the parents in the lobby are the real tryout. Nobody talks, everybody watches through the glass, and one dad is always narrating under his breath like he's calling it on the radio.

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: Seven kids for two spots and he's sleeping nine hours. Whatever happens this weekend, that part can't be coached.

comments.author: zamboni_dreams
comments.body: Tryout weekends are the quietest the stands ever get at our building. You can hear every puck hit the pads from the bay door. Rooting for the calm one.

replies.author: goalie_mom_deb
replies.body: Saturday session done. He came off the ice and asked if we could get pancakes. Pancakes. I have aged a full year and he wants pancakes.

drip.author: penaltyboxphil
drip.title: Find one skate sharpener and stay loyal. Stop letting whoever's working the counter guess your hollow.
drip.body:
Hollow is how deep the groove between your edges is. Smaller number, deeper cut, more bite, more drag. Half inch is where most people start. Heavier skaters often go a bit shallower because they sink in more. Lighter skaters who want grip go deeper.

That's the easy part. The hard part is consistency. A good sharpener does it the same way every time, checks that the edges are level, and remembers you. Find that person. Bring them a coffee in October. Your edges will thank you.

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: I've been asked my hollow at the counter for twenty years and I have answered 'uh, normal' every single time. They always nod like that means something.

replies.author: penaltyboxphil
replies.body: It means half inch. Everyone who says normal gets half inch.

comments.author: zamboni_dreams
comments.body: The ice has a vote too. Soft ice with a deep hollow feels like skating through glue, hard ice with a shallow one feels like a skid. Same skates, different building, different night.

comments.author: portage_and_main
comments.body: The man who sharpened at our old community club worked out of a room the size of a closet with the radio on. Never once asked anybody their hollow. Looked at you, looked at the skates, did it. Nobody ever complained.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: Goalie skates are their own negotiation. He wants them done the day before a game, never the day of. I've driven across town on a weeknight for this more times than I can count. Our sharpener recognizes my car.

replies.author: penaltyboxphil
replies.body: Day before is right. Nobody should be breaking in fresh edges during a game.

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: outdoor rink counterpoint: nobody at shinny knows their hollow and everybody skates fine. but yes, bring the coffee

drip.author: portage_and_main
drip.title: Hockey history from my corner of the map: the first time the Stanley Cup left Montreal, it went to Winnipeg
drip.body:
The Cup was only a few years old when the Winnipeg Victorias went east in the winter of 1896, played the Montreal Victorias, and won 2-0. First team from outside Montreal to take it. The way the story was told to me growing up, folks back home crowded into hotels to hear the result come in by telegraph.

Their goalie, Whitey Merritt, is usually credited as the first to wear cricket pads in a Cup game, and he got the shutout in them. So every time I see a goalie in pads that cost more than my first car, I think about a man in 1896 strapping on cricket gear and deciding that would do. Montreal won it back before the year was out, for the record. We don't dwell on that part.

comments.author: penaltyboxphil
comments.body: Shutout in cricket pads. And we complain about our gear. Good post.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: Saving this for the drive to practice tonight. He's going to ask what the rest of the goalie equipment looked like back then and I'm going to have to admit I have no idea.

replies.author: portage_and_main
replies.body: Report back. If he asks for cricket pads for Christmas, that's between the two of you.

comments.author: crokinole_king
comments.body: Canadiana desk adding one: Lord Stanley's original bowl was bought in London for ten guineas. I think about that every time I see the white gloves come out.

replies.author: elbows_up
replies.body: best return on ten guineas in human history. no notes

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: 'We don't dwell on that part' is the most Winnipeg sentence ever typed, and I mean that as a compliment.

comments.author: zamboni_dreams
comments.body: Natural ice back then. No plant, no machine, just a crew with shovels and water barrels between periods and the weather deciding the rest. I'd have lasted about one period.

drip.author: elbows_up
drip.title: every beer league team is the same eight guys in different jerseys
drip.body:
the guy who's been retiring after this season for nine seasons. the ex-junior guy playing at forty percent who is still the best one out there. the stick taping artist who misses warmup. the ref lawyer. the guy who brought the beer and forgot his skates. the goalie, who is the only one who stretched. the guy who has to leave right at the buzzer. and you.

figure out which one you are before someone tells you

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: I'm the ref lawyer. I've known it for years and made my peace with it. I would also like to appeal this classification.

replies.author: elbows_up
replies.body: appeal denied. two minutes for arguing the call, which you will also argue

comments.author: penaltyboxphil
comments.body: You're missing one. The guy who says 'easy, easy' on every shift like he's calming a horse. Every team has him.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: The goalie being the only one who stretched starts young. My son stretches for twenty minutes in the lobby while his teammates wander in at the last second eating granola bars.

comments.author: portage_and_main
comments.body: I've been the retiring-after-this-season guy since the late nineties. The team threw me a retirement party once. I showed up to the next skate. Nobody was even a little surprised.

replies.author: zamboni_dreams
replies.body: Every building has one. We see the name back on the ice schedule every September and just smile.

drip.author: goalie_mom_deb
drip.title: Arena gear swap morning is the most honest marketplace in the country
drip.body:
Once a year our arena lobby turns into a flea market of hockey bags. Tables of shin pads sorted by size, a mountain of helmets, sticks leaning on every wall with masking tape price tags. My son outgrew his leg pads over the summer, which in goalie terms is a financial event, so we went early with his old set and a hopeful attitude.

Sold his old pads to a family with a nervous eight-year-old who just volunteered to play net. Bought a set one size up, barely used, from a mom whose kid switched to forward after one season. Nobody haggled hard. Everyone just seemed glad the gear was going to another kid.

comments.author: thrifted_thunder
comments.body: Barely used goalie pads from a kid who switched to forward is the holy grail of secondhand anything, and you walked out with it. Triumphant. Swaps and garage sales are where the real deals have always lived.

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: Somewhere on a stick wall like that is a stick I sold years ago with my tape job still on it. I like to think it's scoring more now than it ever did with me.

replies.author: goalie_mom_deb
replies.body: The bar is low, and I say that with love.

comments.author: portage_and_main
comments.body: Masking tape and marker price tags are a national art form. Ours had a whole table labelled 'mystery elbow pads, five bucks, no refunds, no questions.'

comments.author: penaltyboxphil
comments.body: Only thing I won't buy used is a helmet. You don't know where it's been or what it's hit. Everything else, go nuts.

replies.author: zamboni_dreams
replies.body: Swap day is also when our lost and found finally gets emptied. Half the unclaimed gloves in the building end up on a free table by the door.

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: the nervous eight year old who just volunteered for net is wearing your son's old pads now. that's the circle of life and I'm not getting misty at my desk, you are

drip.author: offsidewinger
drip.title: The drive home after the 10:45 skate is the best fifteen minutes of my week
drip.body:
Bag in the back, heat on because it's finally cold enough at midnight to need it, windows cracked anyway because of the bag. Streets empty. Some late-night call-in radio show I'd never admit to listening to anywhere else. Legs done, head quiet.

We lost 5-3, and I'll be reviewing one particular pinch in my sleep, but by the second red light none of it matters. Anyone else get this, or is it just the D-men with nothing left in the tank to think with?

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: the quiet drive is the real third period. nobody talks about it because we're all alone in the car when it happens

comments.author: zamboni_dreams
comments.body: The 10:45 is my last flood of the night. After your lot clears out I do the final lap with the building empty and drive home through the same empty streets. We've probably sat at the same red light.

replies.author: offsidewinger
replies.body: Going to start nodding at every set of headlights just in case.

comments.author: penaltyboxphil
comments.body: The pinch you replay on the drive home is the one you don't make next week. That's how it's supposed to work.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: My version is the 5:40 a.m. drive with a sleeping goalie in the passenger seat and the sun not up yet. Opposite end of the day, exact same quiet.

comments.author: portage_and_main
comments.body: Winnipeg edition: in a couple of months that drive includes a block heater cord and a car that complains for the first three blocks. Still the best fifteen minutes going. Enjoy the fall ones while they last, my friend.

late_comments.author: offsidewinger
late_comments.body: Update for anyone who finds this thread: the kid who deked me signed up for our fall league. He's on my team now. First shift together he gave me a tap on the shin pads and said 'nice to be on the same side, sir.' Still with the sir.

late_comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
late_comments.body: Found this thread while the outdoor rinks are still just empty boards, and I'd like to add the goalie clause: whoever gets voluntold into net picks which end they defend. Small mercy, but it's theirs.

late_comments.author: portage_and_main
late_comments.body: Wandered back to this one after the same argument broke out at the rink canteen. Still Gretzky. For anyone new to the debate, the man scored 50 goals in his first 39 games of a single season. One shift is plenty for a guy like that.
